what: FIS runs the software banks use to keep accounts, process payments and run their branches, and sells capital markets software for trading and treasury operations.
customers: Banks and credit unions of every size, plus asset managers and corporate treasuries.
money: core account processing, digital banking and payments
remaining businesses after the Worldpay separation
moat: Core banking software is the hardest thing in a bank to replace: an account processing migration takes years and risks every customer record, so contracts renew almost automatically.
risks: The Worldpay merger and then separation destroyed a lot of value and the shares are far below their peak
Banks are slow to spend, and the revenue grows only in the low single digits
opportunities: 3.9 times earnings and 4.8 times free cash flow, among the cheapest valuations in payments software
$2.8B of free cash flow against a $13.4B market value
Analysts see about 34% upside, with 23 covering the stock
watch: Recurring revenue growth in Banking Solutions and the pace of debt reduction.
